summary: C2-D042-01 landed in full. Clause 2 now names four unmet items -- fixture execution (DR-G09), join blockers BLK-1/2/3/4 STILL-ROUTED, host-under-instruction outside this vocabulary (D-032), and the FC-C1 host-effect live instance -- and closes with 'This recording discharges none of those.' The alternatives add 'Omit the unmet list. Rejected (C2-D042-01).' I verified each of the four against its governing source rather than against the entry's assertion, and all four are accurate. All six digest recitals reproduce against bytes I measured myself, including my own turn-1 verdict at 61caf972. I ran a token-level diff of turn 1 against turn 2 specifically to catch substance removed during an additive repair, which is the failure mode that has caught me before. One token was genuinely lost: the MF-6 citation. I record it as a NOTE rather than a SHOULD-FIX because the operative sentence survives verbatim and nothing is misrepresented, and I would rather consent than inflate a parenthetical into a blocker.

notesRecorded.observation: The MF-6 citation was dropped during the repair. Turn 1 read 'Does not edit file 08 (MF-6).' Turn 2 reads 'Does not edit file 08.' Measured: MF-6 occurs once in the turn-1 draft and zero times in turn 2.
notesRecorded.whyItIsOnlyANote: The operative statement survives verbatim, the fact it states is true (git reports file 08 unmodified and its live digest matches the recital), and no reader is misled about what the entry does. MF-6 applies to a later register edit whether or not this entry cites it. Raising this to SHOULD-FIX would block CONSENT over a parenthetical, and the repair I asked for landed completely.
notesRecorded.whyItIsWorthRecordingAtAll: D-038, the entry this one cites as its form, spends a whole clause on the point: 'A later file-08 cell note that names this recording is a separate MF-6 act if it changes register content. This entry does not edit file 08.' Once D-042 is adopted, the natural next act is a file-08 cell note naming this recording, and that act is exactly what MF-6 governs. Turn 1 at least pointed at the rule. Restoring the parenthetical, or adopting D-038's fuller forward-warning, costs nothing.
notesRecorded.alsoObserved: My turn-1 remedy suggested adding 'No `docs/v2/implementation/`' to complete the parallel with D-038 clause 3. Turn 2 did not add it. I do not press this: D-035, equally cited, does not carry it either, and clause 4 already carries 'No freeze motion. No blueprint.' Recorded so the omission is visible as a choice rather than an oversight.

consentNote: I CONSENT with zero MUST-FIX and zero SHOULD-FIX, and I state what I attacked. My turn-1 objection was that the entry claimed the D-035/D-038 recording form while omitting that form's defining move -- naming what remains unmet on the row. Turn 2 names four unmet items, attributes each to its governing decision, and adds a blanket 'This recording discharges none of those' that is stronger than what I asked for. I verified all four against D-032, D-038 and file 08's DR-G09 row rather than accepting the entry's word. The one real loss in the repair, the MF-6 citation, does not change what the entry does or authorizes, so it is a note and not a reason to withhold consent.
